title: Buttonhole wheel
subtitle: A circle of buttonhole bars radiating from a central hole to form a flower or eyelet
excerpt: Buttonhole wheel works buttonhole stitch in a circle, with every bar pointing inward toward a shared central hole. The result is a solid ring of upright bars with a neat open centre, used for flower heads, decorative eyelets, and small round motifs in surface embroidery.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), buttonhole stitch and eyelet entries. Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), eyelet and buttonhole wheel entries.

content.text: Buttonhole wheel is buttonhole stitch worked in a ring. Each bar is inserted into the same central hole and emerges on the outer circle, so all bars radiate from one point like spokes. The looped base of each stitch builds up a continuous ridge around the outer edge. The central hole remains open or can be pierced with a stiletto before starting to give a clean eyelet centre.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands; pearl cotton no. 8 for a bold ring

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Firm evenweave linen or cotton; trace the outer circle with a water-soluble pen

items.label: Hoop
items.value: 15 cm hoop to keep the circle evenly taut

content.text: Mark the outer circle and the centre point. Fasten the thread on the back. Bring the needle up at point (A) on the outer circle.

Insert the needle down at the centre point (B). Bring the tip back up at point (C) on the outer circle, one bar-width to the right of (A). Pass the thread under the needle tip before pulling through. The loop locks at the outer rim and forms one bar.

For every subsequent bar, insert the needle into the same centre point (B) and bring it up the next position around the outer circle. Pass the thread under the needle before pulling through each time.
Continue around the full circle, keeping bar height and spacing even. The bars should be close together so the outer ridge forms a solid ring.
When the last bar meets the first, take the needle down into the base of the first loop to close the ring neatly, then fasten off on the back.

items.symptom: The centre hole closes up and disappears
items.cause: Too many bars are converging into the same centre point and the thread bulk fills it.
items.fix: For a clean open centre, pierce the centre with a stiletto before starting and keep bar insertion points within that same hole rather than around it.

items.symptom: Outer ridge is lumpy rather than smooth
items.cause: Bar spacing around the outer circle is uneven.
items.fix: Mark equal-distance points around the outer circle before starting, or count fabric threads for a consistent gap.

items.cause: The last bar is too far from the first.
items.fix: Check the remaining gap against the bar width when about 3 to 4 bars from the start, and adjust spacing slightly across the last few stitches.

content.text: Buttonhole wheel is used for flower centres, standalone round motifs, and decorative eyelets on whitework and broderie anglaise. The ring of bars is built from the same looped motion as
